title: VSift search data v1
description: The data member of a complete or partial search result: one bounded page of the transcript segments that match a literal query, in rank order (phrase matches first, then all-terms matches, each by segment start). items are the matching segments as published transcript evidence records (transcript-segment.schema.json), exactly as transcript.get returns them; hits names each item's segment_id and how it matched, in the same order. query.terms is how the query was normalised. range is the requested range, or null when the whole transcript was searched. transcript_coverage says which parts of the searched range a transcript covers: a word said in an untranscribed range cannot be found. Since 0.3.0 a first page also carries screen_text: the query's occurrences in on-screen text that ocr has read, with its own coverage; on-screen text is never part of items, hits, the cursor or transcript_coverage. Validate the envelope with operation-response.schema.json: its coverage member is truncated, and its status partial, exactly when untranscribed_ranges is not empty. Pass next_cursor back with the same session, query, range and revision to continue; it is rejected for any other search, session or revision, or after the session expires.

screen_text.description: Since 0.3.0 (ADR 0030), on a first page only: the query's occurrences in on-screen text read by ocr, with each hit's frame, time and region, and how much of the searched range's plan is read. Absent on a page a cursor continues and from releases before 0.3.0. It never changes the envelope's status or coverage.

since.description: Since 0.3.0 (ADR 0033): present in every answer to --since, and over an open revision in the answer that ends the read (one without next_cursor; a paged read has it on its last page only). since_token is passed back with --since to read (or search) only what the revision publishes after this answer, in start order; it follows the one revision this answer read until it is sealed or stopped, and expires with the session. revision_state is that revision's state now; more is true when this answer stopped at its limit with more already published after it.

terms.description: The normalised query words, in query order: lowercase letters and digits, with a decimal point only between digits.

match.description: phrase: the query words joined without spaces equal consecutive segment words joined without spaces. all_terms: every query word is a segment word, in any order.

transcript_coverage.description: What a transcript covers of the range a command was asked about: the searched range of a search, or, since 0.2.1, the requested range of a transcript get, by one rule. A word said in an untranscribed range cannot be found by a search and is not shown by a read: an empty page there is a gap, never evidence of silence.

basis.description: supplied_transcript: a supplied SubRip or WebVTT file, taken to cover the whole source but not verified to be complete. local_asr: local speech recognition only; covered ranges are those it examined. mixed: local speech recognition of part of the source spliced into supplied text elsewhere.

scope.description: What this block covers: transcript text only. On-screen text is not counted here; since 0.3.0 a search first page states its coverage in screen_text.coverage.

searched_range.description: The requested range (the whole source for a search with no range) clipped to the source; null when the requested range lies wholly outside it. For a transcript get it is the range of the read, and every page of one request states the same coverage.

no_speech_ranges.description: Transcribed ranges where local recognition found no audible signal, no audio or, since 0.2.0-rc.3, less than 100 ms of audio; never overlapping a segment.

ranges_truncated.description: True when a range list held more than 100 ranges and only its first 100, in start order, are listed.

pending_ranges.description: Since 0.3.0 (ADR 0033): the part of untranscribed_ranges that an open revision will still publish; absent when nothing is pending. A word said there cannot be found yet; that does not mean none was said.

pending_covered_by.description: Since 0.3.0 (ADR 0033): the earlier, sealed revision (the one the open revision supersedes) that still holds text over part of the pending ranges, and those parts; read them with --revision. Absent when there is none.
